bib.title: BERTSCORE: EVALUATING TEXT GENERATION WITH BERT

read.skipped: Tables 12-28 (per-language appendix correlation tables) skimmed only by heading; Tables 29-30 read.

question: Can a metric built from pre-trained contextual token embeddings and greedy matching correlate better with human judgments of generated text than n-gram and other existing metrics?
hypothesis: Contextual-embedding similarity handles paraphrase and word order better than n-gram overlap, so it correlates better with human judgments and is more robust to adversarial paraphrases.
contributions: BERTScore: token-level cosine matching of contextual embeddings with optional idf weighting and baseline rescaling
Evaluation on 363 MT and captioning systems (WMT16-18, COCO 2015) for correlation and model selection
Adversarial paraphrase robustness test on PAWS-QQP
Layer selection per embedding model on WMT16 and an ablation against MoverScore

method.summary: BERTScore embeds reference and candidate tokens with a pre-trained encoder (no training or fine-tuning), computes pairwise cosine similarity, greedily matches each token to its most similar counterpart, and averages to recall, precision and F1, optionally idf-weighted. It is compared to BLEU, ITER, RUSE, YiSi-1 and others on WMT segment/system-level human judgments, COCO captioning, and PAWS-QQP paraphrase detection.
method.task: automatic evaluation of text generation against references (MT, captioning, paraphrase detection)

models.name: Other embedding models (BERT base/large, MRPC, RoBERTa base/MNLI, XLNet, XLM)

inference.samples: Model selection: 100 of 10K hybrid systems ranked, repeated 100K times; otherwise single deterministic scoring

parameters.matching: greedy (max over other sentence tokens), not optimal assignment
parameters.idf: idf(w) = -log (1/M) sum I[w in x(i)] computed on test-set references, plus-one smoothing
parameters.rescaling: (R - b)/(1 - b), b from 1M random Common Crawl pairs; does not change ranking
parameters.layer_per_model: Table 8: roberta-large 17/24, bert-base-uncased 9/12, bert-large-uncased 18/24, multilingual-cased 9/12, bert-base-chinese 8/12, roberta-large-mnli 19/24, xlnet-base 5/12, xlnet-large 7/24
parameters.default_config: no idf after main results ('We continue without idf weighting'), F1 recommended

other.speed: 192.5 pairs/s on GTX-1080Ti; WMT18 en-de test (2,998 sentences) 15.6 s vs 5.4 s SacreBLEU

metrics.name: Absolute Pearson |rho|
metrics.definition: system-level correlation with human judgments; significance by Williams test

metrics.name: Kendall tau
metrics.definition: segment-level rank correlation with human judgments; bootstrap resampling significance

metrics.name: Hits@1
metrics.definition: percent of 100K draws of 100 hybrid systems where the metric's top system equals the human top system

metrics.name: MRR and Diff
metrics.definition: reciprocal rank of metric's top system in human ranking; human score gap between human-best and metric-best system

metrics.name: Pearson on COCO M1, M2
metrics.definition: M1 = percent of captions better or equal to human; M2 = percent indistinguishable from human

metrics.name: AUC
metrics.definition: ROC area for paraphrase detection using the score as classifier

eval.protocol: Layer chosen on WMT16 then fixed; 0.95 CI below 1e-3 for Hits@1; no seeds for BERTScore itself (deterministic).

results.claim: BERTScore F1 beats sentence BLEU at segment level on WMT18 de-en (RoBERTa-large).
results.setup: WMT18 segment-level, 78k German-to-English pairs, F_BERT (no idf and idf both 0.550); BLEU 0.415

results.claim: BERTScore F1 on PAWS-QQP AUC vs BLEU, near chance for BLEU.
results.setup: PAWS-QQP dev (667 sentences), RoBERTa-large F_BERT without idf; idf variant 0.693; BLEU 0.527
results.note: Idf variant 0.693 is the bolded cell

results.claim: R_BERT with idf correlates with COCO M1 human judgments, below LEIC but above SPICE.
Precision-based P_BERT is negatively correlated with COCO M1, F1 only 0.322.
Hits@1 model selection on WMT18 en-de to-English: F_BERT 0.824 vs BLEU 0.803.
BERTScore is fast enough for validation.
results.setup: GTX-1080Ti, WMT18 en-de 2,998 sentences 15.6 s vs 5.4 s SacreBLEU
results.quote: We are able to process 192.5 candidate-reference pairs/second using a GTX-1080Ti GPU.

results.claim: Best layer for RoBERTa-large is 17 of 24; correlation drops sharply in final layers.
results.note: Fig 3 caption: 'correlation drops significantly in the final layers'

results.claim: Replacing greedy matching with WMD does not consistently improve BERTScore.
results.setup: WMT17 to-English segment-level, 12-layer uncased BERT, Table 9

results.claim: BERTScore recall correlates with MSR compression meaning judgments.
results.setup: MSR Abstractive Text Compression, meaning scores; BLEU 0.46

limits: No single configuration wins everywhere; the authors say users must weigh model, language and domain.
Fails on factual errors (English for German, Tuesday for Monday) and unit equivalences like 5ft 11in vs 1.80 metres (Appendix A).
idf weighting helps only at times; the authors defer when to future work.
Less stable on low-resource languages with multilingual BERT.
Needs a reference; evidence is MT, captioning, paraphrase detection and one compression set, not open-ended generation.
Precision and F1 are poor for COCO captioning; recall is best.
Layer was tuned on WMT16, the same data family as the test years.
